title: Customer escalation war-room - Beta Retail (prep + notes)
content:
Context:
- Beta Retail (customer: Beta Retail Inc.) seeing intermittent 500s and high latency for embed+search flow since 2026-03-07 18:00 UTC. Issue spikes during catalog syncs (daily batch). Impact: search returns failing for some users; customer reports increased error rate ~12% on peak syncs (severity: potential revenue impact).

Purpose of this doc:
- Prep notes for the escalation war-room meeting (standup + triage)
- Capture real-time notes and assign follow-ups

Attendees (requested):
- Maya Chen (CS lead, owner)
- Ethan Brooks (SRE)
- Samiya Rao (Serving runtime eng)
- Ben Kaplan (Solutions Eng / on-call for Beta Retail)
- Alex Rivera (Customer engineering contact at Beta Retail) - optional

Agenda (30 min):
1) Quick context & status (Maya, 3m)
2) Recent telemetry summary (Ethan, 5m)
3) Repro/first-failure timeline & suspected root causes (Samiya, 7m)
4) Immediate mitigation options & rollback plan (Ben, 7m)
5) Communication plan with customer + next steps (Maya, 4m)
6) Action item assignment (2m)

Recent telemetry highlights (to pull before call):
- Error spikes correlate with catalog sync windows at ~02:00 PT and ~20:00 PT.
- Top error: 500 from inference service chain (model routing) + timeouts from dedicated pool.
- CPU/GPU utilization: GPUs not saturated; some workers report KV cache evictions concurrent with sync.
- Redis cache miss ratio increased from 2% -> 12% during window.
- Region: US-west primarily.

Immediate hypotheses:
- Cache stampede due to sync causing many cold prefix requests (missing prefix/KV cache).
- Autoscaling config not responding quickly enough to burst of short-lived requests.
- Model routing fallback to slower variant under load causing timeouts.

Mitigation options (fast to implement):
- Option A: Temporarily throttle catalog syncs on Beta Retail side (ask customer to stagger or pause syncs for 2 windows).
- Option B: Apply short-term cache priming for known prefixes prior to sync window (solutions eng script).
- Option C: Increase autoscaling headroom for dedicated pool (SRE action, may be gated by quota).
- Option D: Force route to primary model variant with higher throughput (runtime change, risk: cost).

Communication drafts (to send post-meeting):
- 1) Acknowledgement: we are aware and triaging; ETA for mitigation suggestion in 30m; next update in 2 hours.
- 2) Follow-up after mitigation: summary of actions taken, expected customer-visible impact, and next steps.

Known constraints / risks:
- Changing autoscaling may affect other tenants if Dedicated pool is shared; need to confirm isolation.
- Forcing model variant could increase latency for other queries; coordinate with product if cost/sla implications.

Notes (live):
- 09:03 Maya: started war-room, pulled error graphs (Ethan).
- 09:05 Ethan: confirmed Redis misses + worker restarts correlated with errors; attached logs in JIRA-4821.
- 09:07 Samiya: KV cache eviction threshold reached because of frequent new prefixes during sync; root cause likely sync pattern creating many unique prompts.
- 09:11 Ben: solutions eng prepared cache-priming script prototype; can run dry-run in staging.
- 09:14 Decision: run cache-priming for next sync and ask Beta Retail to pause non-essential sync jobs for next 1 window if possible.

Action items (owner - due):
- Ethan Brooks - run deep log correlation and surface top-5 failing call stacks; attach to JIRA-4821 - due 2026-03-09 13:00
- Ben Kaplan - run cache-priming dry-run in staging and prepare safe rollout playbook (include rollback) - due 2026-03-09 14:30
- Maya Chen - coordinate ask with Beta Retail (pause non-critical syncs) and send acknowledgement email + RCA timeline - due 2026-03-09 09:30 (sent)
- Samiya Rao - validate autoscaling config for dedicated pool and simulate burst to confirm scaling latency; flag any config changes needed - due 2026-03-10 11:00
- Alex Rivera (Beta Retail) - confirm they can pause/schedule syncs and provide list of critical syncs - due 2026-03-09 10:00
- Maya Chen & Ben Kaplan - if cache-priming looks good, schedule production run with Beta Retail for next sync window and monitor - tentative due 2026-03-09 20:30

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we have historical prefix distribution for Beta Retail to precompute priming? (Samiya to check)
- Is dedicated pool truly isolated for Beta Retail or shared across small accounts? (Ethan to confirm infra config)
- If priming fails, fallback plan = throttle syncs + increase headroom (need customer buy-in).

Attachments & quick refs:
- JIRA-4821: primary incident ticket (logs + graphs)
- JIRA-4822: customer communication thread
- Slack thread: #cust-beta-retail (link above)

Follow-up cadence:
- 2-hour update after initial mitigation; then daily until resolved.
- Postmortem scheduled tentative 2026-03-12 (owner: Maya Chen).

Notes to self:
- Keep communication high bandwidth with Beta Retail; assign a single POC (Alex) for approvals.
- If root cause confirmed as prefix explosion, consider long-term fix: client-side deduping or server-side prefetch and more aggressive KV cache retention for long-tail prefixes.
- Draft postmortem template early so we can iterate with eng and customer-success before finalizing.

End of doc.
